markdownRemark.html:
1. Architecture Design

Redis

  • In-Memory Storage: Redis primarily stores data in memory, resulting in extremely low read/write latency.
  • Data Persistence: It supports both RDB snapshots and AOF logs, allowing flexible switching between memory and disk storage.
  • Rich Data Types: Redis offers a variety of data structures, including strings, lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes, bitmaps, HyperLogLog, and geospatial indexes.
  • Single-Threaded Model: By using a single-threaded event loop, Redis ensures atomic operations and avoids concurrency conflicts.
  • Replication and Clustering: It supports master–slave replication, sentinel mode, and cluster architecture, making it suitable for high availability and distributed environments.

ValkeyDB

  • Memory Mapping and Disk Persistence: ValkeyDB uses memory mapping (mmap) to directly access disk data, balancing in-memory performance with persistence needs.
  • Lightweight Design: It strikes a balance between data persistence and fast access, making it ideal for scenarios with large data volumes that require efficient disk reads.
  • Simplified Data Model: Compared to Redis’s rich set of data types, ValkeyDB focuses on efficient key–value storage and fast querying.

2. Performance Metrics

Throughput

  • Redis:
    • Read Operations: In a typical single-node environment, Redis can achieve 100k–200k operations per second.
    • Write Operations: Write throughput is generally between 80k–150k operations per second, depending on the persistence configuration and data scale.
  • ValkeyDB:
    • Read Operations: In persistent mode, ValkeyDB’s read throughput is usually around 100k–150k operations per second.
    • Write Operations: Write throughput ranges from 80k to 120k operations per second, slightly lower than Redis due to disk synchronization and consistency requirements.

Latency

  • Redis:
    • Since operations are entirely in memory, read/write latency typically ranges from 0.1 to 1 ms.
  • ValkeyDB:
    • Read latency is generally between 0.5 to 1 ms, and write latency falls between 1 to 2 ms, slightly higher than pure in-memory operations due to disk I/O.

3. Data Consistency and Persistence

  • Redis:
    • Supports both RDB snapshots and AOF logs, ensuring high availability and disaster recovery.
    • Data is entirely stored in memory, making it suitable for applications with extremely high responsiveness requirements, although memory capacity can be a limitation.
  • ValkeyDB:
    • Uses memory mapping to directly access disk data, providing inherent advantages in persistence and data recovery.
    • More suitable for scenarios with large data volumes and high requirements for data consistency and efficient disk reads.

4. Use Cases and Applicability

  • Redis Use Cases:

    • Caching: With its extremely low latency and high throughput, Redis is commonly used to cache hot data.
    • Real-Time Data Processing: Ideal for message queues, real-time leaderboards, session management, etc.
    • Distributed Locks and Counters: Its single-threaded model and rich data types make Redis excellent for implementing distributed locks and counters.

  • ValkeyDB Use Cases:

    • Large-Scale Data Storage: When data volumes exceed available memory, ValkeyDB’s direct disk access via memory mapping offers better scalability.
    • High Persistence Requirements: Suitable for applications that demand high data consistency and persistence.
    • Cost-Effective Deployment: Provides a balanced solution for environments where upgrading hardware memory is not feasible.

5. Summary

Metric Redis ValkeyDB
Architecture In-memory storage, rich data types, single-threaded event model Memory mapping + disk persistence, lightweight key–value storage
Read Throughput 100k–200k ops/sec 100k–150k ops/sec
Write Throughput 80k–150k ops/sec 80k–120k ops/sec
Read Latency 0.1–1 ms 0.5–1 ms
Write Latency 1–2 ms 1–2 ms
Persistence RDB and AOF, hybrid in-memory and disk storage Direct disk access via memory mapping
Use Cases Caching, real-time processing, distributed locks Large-scale storage, high persistence needs, resource-constrained environments

Redis, with its extremely high throughput and very low latency, is ideal for in-memory caching scenarios where response time is critical. In contrast, ValkeyDB offers a more cost-effective solution for scenarios with large data volumes that require efficient persistence and direct disk-based reads.

In practice, the choice should be based on the specific requirements, data scale, and hardware configuration of your application. It is even advisable to conduct benchmark tests in the target environment to determine the optimal solution.

frontmatter.title: Valkey vs Redis Technical Comparison
frontmatter.description: In modern distributed systems and caching applications, the choice of a data storage solution is critical to system performance and stability. This article provides a comparative analysis of two commonly used data storage solutions — Redis and ValkeyDB (referred to as Valkey) — focusing on their technical specifications. The goal is to help developers understand their respective advantages and suitable scenarios.
